assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new quantum state of matter platform: moire flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in a simple carbon system, which also reopens the lesson from graphene that experiment can overturn expectations. A clean case of theory predicting a non-obvious band structure and experiment delivering a surprising phase diagram.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the magic-angle prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. Two or three of the credited names is a natural configuration; I would include Bistritzer for the theory but accept MacDonald plus Jarillo-Herrero if the committee wants two. Experimental credit may also extend to collaborators not on the list, which I cannot assess.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups across devices and techniques, and the band-structure picture is supported by spectroscopy and ab initio-informed models. Interpretation of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the core discovery is robust and timely.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Whether other experimental contributors have comparable claims to credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ARPES is the direct experimental window onto the electronic structure that my own theory tries to compute, and it has shaped understanding of cuprates, topological materials and correlated systems. It is a measurement technique with decades of quantitative impact, close to the way theory and spectroscopy interact in practice.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano and Shen are central to the modern high-resolution ARPES of correlated materials; Johnson is credited for spin- and angle-resolved developments. I would restrict the proposal to two names, though an allocation between technique development and its scientific applications is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Method is long established, widely used at synchrotrons and independently reproduced. Recognition is arguably overdue, though the prize needs a framing as an instrument or technique with discoveries, not a general field.
uncertainties: Who contributed the decisive instrumental advances versus applications is diffuse.
Past committees may regard it as a cumulative technique rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states; theory predicted them and experiment confirmed them in HgTe and Bi-based materials, with spectroscopic proof by ARPES. Exactly the kind of verified discovery with theory-experiment dialogue that I value.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe, and Hasan's ARPES work established 3D topological insulators. Three names is workable (Kane, Molenkamp, Hasan) but it leaves out Mele, and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu-Kane-Mele contributions are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive, the interpretation is stable and the field is mature; the 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions, so the committee would need to articulate the distinct contribution.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and with related quantum anomalous Hall and quantum spin Hall candidates.
Fair allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and unlisted theorists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT is the leading framework for strongly correlated materials, linking model Hamiltonians to real-material electronic structure via DFT+DMFT. It transformed how Mott physics and correlated oxides are computed and compared with spectra, and I know its practical power well.
assessment.attribution: Metzner-Vollhardt established the infinite-dimension limit, Georges-Kotliar built the mapping to impurity models and the practical method. The three credited names are a coherent set, though the contribution of Metzner and others is not on the list and credit is genuinely shared.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use and validation against experiment. A theoretical method prize needs a clear physical discovery at the centre, and the committee may see it as a tool rather than a discovery.
uncertainties: Whether a methods prize fits the criteria.
Credit to unlisted contributors such as Metzner.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nd2Fe14B magnets underpin wind turbines, electric motors and data storage, and are the clearest case of magnetic materials physics meeting sustainable energy. The invention is of enormous practical consequence, which I value, though the underlying physics is established magnetism rather than a new phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (Sumitomo) and Croat (General Motors) discovered the compound independently and almost simultaneously in 1983, so a two-person prize is natural, though it would need to handle the independent-discovery and the corporate-patent history carefully.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use; the structure and properties are thoroughly confirmed by theory and neutron experiments. Recognition is mature if not late.
uncertainties: Whether an invention of material with modest new physics matches the intent of the physics prize.
Priority and patent disputes between the two discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance made magnetic tunnel junctions the basis of hard-disk read heads and MRAM, a case where spin-dependent quantum tunnelling becomes technology. The physics is well explained by theory, including coherent tunnelling in MgO.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki reported room-temperature TMR in 1995 and Parkin later developed the MgO-based high-TMR devices. The three-name set is fair, though the theoretical prediction of MgO symmetry filtering (Butler, Mathon) is outside the list, and 2007 GMR prize overlap is relevant.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and independently confirmed. Because the 2007 prize recognised GMR, the committee may see the incremental novelty as lower.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third class of collinear magnetism with spin-split bands without net magnetization, a genuinely new conceptual category in my own field. It is directly connected to computed band structures and to ARPES and magnetotransport evidence.
assessment.attribution: The Prague and Mainz group, with Šmejkal, Jungwirth and Sinova, formulated the classification and its consequences; independent related contributions from other groups exist but are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Recent, with growing but still limited independent experimental confirmation of key signatures. Probably premature for this cycle even though it is promising.
uncertainties: Experimental confirmation is young and the range of material realizations is still being established.
Priority with other proposals on spin-split antiferromagnets.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fractional (anyonic) statistics is a deep quantum surprise: particle exchange statistics beyond bosons and fermions, predicted in 1977 and now observed in interferometry and collision experiments in fractional quantum Hall systems. It fits the theme that quantum mechanics keeps producing surprises.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim made the original prediction in two dimensions; Heiblum's group provided key experimental work, with Fève, Manfra and Rosenow also credited. With six names, a two or three person prize would leave out significant contributors, and the theory credit also overlaps with Wilczek and Halperin, who are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation arrived only in the last few years and independent replication is still limited, so the case is promising but possibly early.
uncertainties: Whether interferometer results are fully free of alternative interpretations.
Difficult credit allocation across six credited names and unlisted theorists.
